subject.title: [Bug]: macOS app 'Launch at login' stops sticking / appears to turn itself off after app updates

question: Should the macOS app persist OpenClaw-owned Launch at login intent and reconcile app-owned LaunchAgent drift after updates, or should live launchd/System Settings state remain authoritative?
rationale: Current code treats live launchd state as the UI source of truth, while the report asks for enabled user intent to survive app replacement and update-time LaunchAgent drift; changing that affects user control and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Persist intent and reconcile app-owned drift
options.body: Store explicit in-app enablement and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

options.title: Keep launchd authoritative
options.body: Leave live launchd and System Settings state as the source of truth and document that OpenClaw will not restore externally disabled login items.

options.title: Wait for packaged update proof
options.body: Keep the issue parked until a current-main Sparkle update repro identifies exactly which launchd or UI state flips.

recommendation.title: Persist intent and reconcile app-owned drift
recommendation.body: Store explicit in-app enablement and re-register only the app-owned LaunchAgent after startup or update drift, with guards for deliberate external disables.

likelyOwner.reason: The feature history points most strongly to steipete for the macOS app launch-at-login source-of-truth choice.
